newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Three S.Korean firms apply for bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Three S.Korean firms apply for bourse listing.

text.p: South Korea's Securities Supervisory Board said on Wednesday three firms have applied to be listed on the Korea Stock Exchange.
If Comtec Systems Co Ltd, Sung Jin Machinery Co Ltd and Woo Bang Housing and Construction Co Ltd pass requirements for initial public offerings, the shares will begin trading in early 1997.
Comtek plans to offer 520,000 shares at 40,000 won per share, underwritten by Daewoo Securities.
Sung Jin hopes to launch a 364,000-share offering at 19,000 won per share. Hyundai Securities will be the lead manager.
Woo Bang plans to offer 3,204,583 shares at 12,000 won per share. Commercial Securities will be the lead manager.

The SSB said that this year, as of October 1, 19 companies have gone public. An additional 12 have held their initial public offerings and will begin trading this year, and 11 are preparing to hold IPOs.
The stock market will see a total of 1.408 trillion won injected into the market from these offerings.
